classification.difficultyReason: Translate comparison-line gradients into derivative conditions. The normal requires a perpendicular-gradient step and reconstruction of its equation, while the trigonometric part requires finding every solution across the transformed interval.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the coordinates of the points on the curve $y=2x^3-2x^2$ where the tangent is parallel to the line $2x-y-5=0$.

answer.worked:
The line is $y=2x-5$, so the required tangent gradient is $2$.

$$\begin{align*}\frac{dy}{dx}&=6x^2-4x\\6x^2-4x&=2\\3x^2-2x-1&=0\\(3x+1)(x-1)&=0.\end{align*}$$

Hence $x=-\frac13$ or $x=1$. Substitute each value into the curve equation.

$$\begin{align*}y\big|_{x=-\frac13}&=2\left(-\frac13\right)^3-2\left(-\frac13\right)^2\\y\big|_{x=-\frac13}&=-\frac{8}{27}\\y\big|_{x=1}&=2(1)^3-2(1)^2\\y\big|_{x=1}&=0.\end{align*}$$

The points are $\left(-\frac13,-\frac{8}{27}\right)$ and $(1,0)$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the equation of the normal to $y=2x^2-3$ that is parallel to $x-y+4=0$.

answer.worked:
The line is $y=x+4$, so the normal has gradient $1$. The tangent has gradient $-1$ because it is perpendicular to the normal.

$$\begin{align*}\frac{dy}{dx}&=4x\\4x&=-1\\x&=-\frac14\\y&=2\left(-\frac14\right)^2-3\\y&=-\frac{23}{8}.\end{align*}$$

Use gradient $1$ and the point $\left(-\frac14,-\frac{23}{8}\right)$.

$$\begin{align*}y+\frac{23}{8}&=x+\frac14\\y&=x-\frac{21}{8}\\8x-8y-21&=0.\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find the point(s) on $y=\cos(3x)-1$ over the domain $x\in[0,\pi]$, where the tangent is parallel to $3x+y=0$.

answer.worked:
The required tangent gradient is $-3$, since the line is $y=-3x$.

$$\begin{align*}\frac{dy}{dx}&=-3\sin(3x)\\-3\sin(3x)&=-3\\\sin(3x)&=1.\end{align*}$$

Since $0\leq 3x\leq 3\pi$, the solutions are $3x=\frac{\pi}{2}$ and $3x=\frac{5\pi}{2}$. Thus $x=\frac{\pi}{6}$ or $x=\frac{5\pi}{6}$. At both values, $\cos(3x)=0$, so $y=-1$.

The points are $\left(\frac{\pi}{6},-1\right)$ and $\left(\frac{5\pi}{6},-1\right)$.
